title: Finding Things
story: You're building a search feature for a contact list. A user types a name — your code needs to find it in the list or report 'not found.' No crashes, no cryptic numbers — just a clean answer.
why: Search operations are the classic use case for Option — you either find what you're looking for (Some) or you don't (None), and the type system enforces handling both cases.
analogy: Finding with Option is like asking a librarian for a book — they either come back with the book in hand (Some) or tell you 'we don't have it' (None).
try_it: Add two more students to find_grade. Then create a `find_honor_roll` function that returns Option[Str] — only return Some(name) for students with A or B. Returns None for C or not found. Test all cases.
tips: Return Some early when you find a match — the rest of the function becomes the 'not found' path
Chain multiple if-checks for a simple lookup table without needing arrays or maps
Use if let when you need special handling for found vs. not found, .unwrap_or for simple defaults
common_mistakes: Continuing to check after returning Some — `return Some(x)` exits the function immediately
Returning `Some("Not found")` — defeats the purpose! Use None for 'not found' so callers can distinguish
Hardcoding a single match check when multiple items could match — consider which result should take priority
